title: Open Tree of Life web services
note: Topology and taxonomy context; divergence dates require separate evidence.

title: Using Phylogenomic Data to Explore the Effects of Relaxed Clocks and Calibration Strategies on Divergence Time Estimation: Primates as a Test Case
authors: dos Reis, M.; Gunnell, G.F.; Barba-Montoya, J.; Wilkins, A.; Yang, Z.; Yoder, A.D.
note: Open manuscript is available through PMC6005039. Node ages are Bayesian model outputs and vary with fossil-calibration strategy and relaxed-clock model.

title: Oldest known euarchontan tarsals and affinities of Paleocene Purgatorius to Primates
authors: Chester, S.G.B.; Bloch, J.I.; Boyer, D.M.; Clemens, W.A.
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: Open version of record at PMC4321231. The tarsals are isolated and attributed to Purgatorius by size, abundance and comparative morphology rather than dental association.

title: Altiatlasius koulchii n. gen. et sp., primate omomyidé du Paléocène supérieur du Maroc, et les origines des Euprimates
authors: Sigé, B.; Jaeger, J.-J.; Sudre, J.; Vianey-Liaud, M.
note: No DOI was located for the original description. The type series is about ten isolated teeth from Adrar Mgorn 1; tooth-locus assignments and broader placement have remained disputed.

title: A new family of plesiadapiformes (Mammalia) from the Old World lower Paleogene
authors: Hooker, J.J.; Russell, D.E.; Phélizon, A.
note: This primary systematic analysis recovers Altiatlasius within Toliapinidae rather than Euprimates. It is included as an explicit alternative placement, not as a replacement for the DOI-less original description.

title: Rapid Asia–Europe–North America geographic dispersal of earliest Eocene primate Teilhardina during the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum
authors: Smith, T.; Rose, K.D.; Gingerich, P.D.
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: Open version of record at PMC1544069. The dispersal sequence is inferred from separate dental samples and intercontinental carbon-isotope correlation.

title: Evidence for a Grooming Claw in a North American Adapiform Primate: Implications for Anthropoid Origins
authors: Maiolino, S.A.; Boyer, D.M.; Bloch, J.I.; Gilbert, C.C.; Groenke, J.
note: Open-access version of record. The grooming-claw diagnosis is a comparative functional inference from preserved phalanges and statistical analyses.

title: Complete Primate Skeleton from the Middle Eocene of Messel in Germany: Morphology and Paleobiology
authors: Franzen, J.L.; Gingerich, P.D.; Habersetzer, J.; Hurum, J.H.; von Koenigswald, W.; Smith, B.H.
note: Open-access version of record at PMC2683573. PMO 214.214 and WDC-MG-210 are part and counterpart of one skeleton; the paper discloses fabricated preparation around portions of the counterplate.

title: The oldest known anthropoid postcranial fossils and the early evolution of higher primates
authors: Gebo, D.L.; Dagosto, M.; Beard, K.C.; Qi, T.; Wang, J.
note: The paper describes isolated Shanghuang tarsals and a Yuanqu talus attributed to eosimiids; none is dentally associated with Eosimias.

title: New Oligocene primate from Saudi Arabia and the divergence of apes and Old World monkeys
authors: Zalmout, I.S.; Sanders, W.J.; MacLatchy, L.M.; Gunnell, G.F.; Al-Mufarreh, Y.A.; Ali, M.A.; Nasser, A.-A.H.; Al-Masari, A.M.; Al-Sobhi, S.A.; Nadhra, A.O.; Matari, A.H.; Wilson, J.A.; Gingerich, P.D.
note: The holotype is one partial cranium. Its 29–28 Ma age is biochronological and its stem-catarrhine position is a morphology-matrix result.

title: Postcranial functional morphology of Morotopithecus bishopi, with implications for the evolution of modern ape locomotion
authors: MacLatchy, L.; Gebo, D.; Kityo, R.; Pilbeam, D.
note: MUZM 60 is from Moroto I and MUZM 80 from Moroto II. Their attribution and locomotor reconstruction are locality-level comparative interpretations, not one skeleton or observed behaviour.

title: A Complete Skull from Dmanisi, Georgia, and the Evolutionary Biology of Early Homo
authors: Lordkipanidze, D.; Ponce de León, M.S.; Margvelashvili, A.; Rak, Y.; Rightmire, G.P.; Vekua, A.; Zollikofer, C.P.E.
note: D4500 and D2600 are associated as Skull 5. The broad single-lineage interpretation of early Homo is an analysis of variation and remains distinct from the specimen observation.

title: A high-coverage Neandertal genome from Vindija Cave in Croatia
authors: Prüfer, K.; de Filippo, C.; Grote, S.; Mafessoni, F.; Korlević, P.; Hajdinjak, M.; Vernot, B.; Skov, L.; Hsieh, P.; Peyrégne, S.; et al.
note: Open manuscript at PMC6185897. The specimen has a direct radiocarbon lower bound; the approximately 52 ka age and demographic histories are genome-based model estimates.

title: Genome sequence of a 45,000-year-old modern human from western Siberia
authors: Fu, Q.; Li, H.; Moorjani, P.; Jay, F.; Slepchenko, S.M.; Bondarev, A.A.; Johnson, P.L.F.; Aximu-Petri, A.; Prüfer, K.; de Filippo, C.; et al.
note: Open manuscript at PMC4753769. PRJEB6622 contains the sequence data; the date is direct radiocarbon calibration, whereas ancestry and admixture timing are model estimates.
